I added `latestForCustomer(String customerId)` to `OrderFacade`. It returns `Optional<OrderSummary>`, so an empty result means the customer has no orders. The full test suite passes.

- **`OrderFacade`**: new method with a Javadoc comment saying what empty means.
- **`OrderRepository`**: `latestFor(customerId)` picks the order with the greatest `placedAt` among that customer's orders. It picks by placement time, not insertion order.
- **`OrderService`**: implements the method as a read-only transaction and maps the result to an `OrderSummary`.
- **`ShopFlowTest`**: two new tests. One checks that a customer with no orders gets an empty result. The other checks that the most recently placed order is returned even when it was inserted first.

# Shop

A modular monolith: `orders`, `payments`, `customers`, `notifications`, `shipping`. Spring wires it; the repositories keep data in memory.

Run the tests with the `run_tests` tool.

The `OrderFacade` interface has one implementation and no test fakes, so adding a method is safe. I'll return `Optional<OrderSummary>` so an empty result is explicit, and pick the latest order by `placedAt` in the repository.
Now I'll add a test covering the main cases: no orders, a single order, and picking the latest by time rather than insertion order.

I added `latestForCustomer(String customerId)` to `OrderFacade`. It returns `Optional<OrderSummary>`, so an empty result means the customer has no orders. The full test suite passes.

- **`OrderFacade`**: new method with a Javadoc comment saying what empty means.
- **`OrderRepository`**: `latestFor(customerId)` picks the order with the greatest `placedAt` among that customer's orders. It picks by placement time, not insertion order.
- **`OrderService`**: implements the method as a read-only transaction and maps the result to an `OrderSummary`.
- **`ShopFlowTest`**: two new tests. One checks that a customer with no orders gets an empty result. The other checks that the most recently placed order is returned even when it was inserted first.
